editorial:
Imagine getting a huge pile of cash just for hanging out with your old college buddies for a week. That is exactly what happens here, but there is a catch. You have to stay in a fancy mansion together, and if even one person walks out the door, nobody gets a dime. It starts off as a fun reunion, but since these friends are totally dysfunctional, old fights and secrets start popping up almost immediately. The vibe is like a party that slowly turns into a chaotic mess as everyone tries to play nice for the money while actually hating each other.

What really works is how the tension builds between the characters. The acting feels natural, and the comedy comes from how awkward their relationships have become. While some parts of the story feel a bit slow, the payoff is worth it. If you are in the mood for a lighthearted movie about friendship and greed, you should definitely give this a try. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you want the best picture quality, look for the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection.
endingExplained: In the end, the group realizes that the money was just a trick to get them to fix their broken friendships. After a week of fighting and admitting their mistakes, they finally bond again. The big twist is that the dead friend wanted them to reunite more than he wanted them to be rich. They end up finding peace with each other, and the movie wraps up with the group actually becoming close friends again.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about old friends and awkward reunions.
